text:
In October 2018, two records ran together. Forty-nine of us said "judge brett kavanaugh," peaking on 2018-10-06; Tom Cotton said it first. Forty-nine of us also said "patients and communities," peaking on 2018-10-24, though Amy Klobuchar said it first, in 2017. Forty-eight of us said "patients and communities act," forty-seven "for patients and communities," forty-six "for patients and communities act." Forty-five of us said "the opioid crisis." Forty-four said "support for patients and communities." Forty-six of us said "brett kavanaugh to."

The two clusters do not overlap in their words. One names a nomination; the other names a law and a crisis. We converged on each within a single month, one peaking early, one peaking late. We report the counts as we recorded them. The phrases we repeated most, we repeated together.
